help.title: Help
help.fallback: No help is available for this page yet.
help.dashboard: Summarizes the current state of your VPN infrastructure: alerts, nodes with issues, traffic per node, recent activity, online users, and pending approval requests. Refreshes automatically every 30 seconds.
help.nodes: Manage your VPN nodes. Use Create node to issue a registration token for a new node, and review each node’s status, resource usage, traffic, and connection count.
help.nodeGroups: Group nodes so plans can target them. A plan bound to a group offers only that group’s nodes to its users.
help.nodeChains: Manage Entry port-to-Exit maps and plan route assignments. Saved configuration is separate from applied policy and subscriber availability.
help.users: Manage VPN users. Review each user’s plan, traffic usage, and device count, and create or edit accounts.
help.plans: Define the plans offered to users: traffic limit, concurrent connections, and which node groups are available.
help.announcements: Write announcements shown in the user portal. You can set the active state and an expiry date.
help.settings: Change panel-wide settings, including operational items such as backups and retention windows.
help.twoFactor: Set up two-factor authentication for the admin account. Once enabled, login also requires a code from your authenticator app.
help.connections: Shows every session currently connected to the VPN: which user, on which device, to which node, and from which address. Users past their concurrent-connection allowance are flagged. Refreshes every 30 seconds.
help.uuidEvictions: Review UUID slot evictions, per-Exit closure acknowledgments, and Exits still pending. Unconfirmed bans are never released automatically.
help.alerts: Every alert that needs action, plus the nodes reporting a problem. Select a node name to open its detail page.
help.activity: The activity log recorded across the panel and the nodes. Filter by severity or activity type.
help.inbounds: Manage this node's inbounds (protocol and port), issue TLS certificates, and update the Xray core. A node serves one protocol at a time.
help.orders: Review plan orders and confirm payment. Marking an order paid applies the plan to the user immediately.
help.promotions: Create and manage promotion codes. A code can cap total and per-user redemptions, apply only to selected plans or durations, require a minimum order, or be limited to first purchases.
help.subscriptionDomains: Manage public subscription domains and review service-side DNS, TLS, and certificate health.
help.resetTickets: Grant data reset tickets and review past grants. Tickets can go to one user, everyone currently on a plan, or every account. Users spend a ticket on their dashboard to reset this month's data usage to zero.
help.support: Read and answer tickets from users. Replying sends the user an email notification.
help.supportHelp: Manage the categories and frequently asked questions shown before a user opens a ticket. Each can be written in Korean, English and Chinese.
help.routing: Edit the proxy groups, rule sets and rule order served in Clash Meta subscriptions. Changes apply on the next subscription refresh.
help.admins: Invite admins, manage their roles and status, and change your own name and password. Only owners can manage other admins.

settings.title: Clash settings
settings.description: Ports, DNS and sniffer options of the generated Clash Meta (mihomo) profile, applied to every user's subscription. The grey text under each field is the real YAML key.

mixed_port.label: Mixed port
mixed_port.desc: Accepts HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy traffic on one port. Point apps and browsers at this port; most clients need only this. 0 disables it.

port.label: HTTP proxy port
port.desc: HTTP-only proxy port. Usually unnecessary when the mixed port is set. 0 disables it.

socks_port.label: SOCKS5 proxy port
socks_port.desc: SOCKS5-only proxy port. Usually unnecessary when the mixed port is set. 0 disables it.

mode.label: Mode
mode.desc: rule: route by the rules below (recommended). global: send everything through the GLOBAL group. direct: connect everything directly without a proxy.

log_level.label: Log level
log_level.desc: How much the client logs. silent logs nothing; debug is the most verbose. Use warning normally and info/debug only when troubleshooting.

find_process_mode.label: Process lookup
find_process_mode.desc: Finds which app opened a connection so PROCESS-NAME rules can match. off: disabled (best for battery). strict: only when process rules exist. always: every connection. Use off on mobile.

allow_lan.label: Allow LAN
allow_lan.desc: Lets other devices on the same Wi-Fi or router use this device's proxy ports. Turn it off on public networks.

bind_address.label: Bind address
bind_address.desc: Which local address listens when LAN access is on. * means all addresses; enter one IP to listen on a single interface.

ipv6.label: IPv6
ipv6.desc: Allows IPv6 connections. When off, IPv6 destinations are blocked and only IPv4 is used. Keep it off if nodes or networks have weak IPv6 support.

unified_delay.label: Unified delay
unified_delay.desc: Measures node latency without handshake overhead, so nodes with different protocols compare fairly and url-test groups pick more accurately.

tcp_concurrent.label: TCP concurrent
tcp_concurrent.desc: When a domain resolves to several IPs, dials them all at once and keeps the fastest. Speeds up first connections.

keep_alive_interval.label: Keep-alive interval (s)
keep_alive_interval.desc: How often a keep-alive probe is sent. Shorter detects dead connections faster but uses more battery. 0 uses the default (15s).

keep_alive_idle.label: Keep-alive idle (s)
keep_alive_idle.desc: Idle seconds before keep-alive probes start. 0 uses the default.

disable_keep_alive.label: Disable keep-alive
disable_keep_alive.desc: Turns TCP keep-alive off completely. Saves battery on mobile, but dead connections are noticed later.

external_controller.label: External controller
external_controller.desc: API address that dashboards (yacd, metacubexd) and apps use to control the client. 127.0.0.1 keeps it local to the device. Empty disables it.

secret.label: Controller secret
secret.desc: Password required by the external controller API. Always set it if the controller listens beyond 127.0.0.1. Every user's profile gets the same value.

store_selected.label: Remember selected nodes
store_selected.desc: Remembers the node a user picked in select groups, so the choice survives restarts.

store_fake_ip.label: Persist fake-IP
store_fake_ip.desc: Saves the domain-to-fake-IP table in fake-IP mode, so existing connections break less after a restart.

geodata_mode.label: Geodata mode
geodata_mode.desc: Use .dat files for GEOIP/GEOSITE rules instead of mmdb. This profile uses rule sets (.mrs), so it can normally stay off.

geo_auto_update.label: Auto-update geo data
geo_auto_update.desc: Periodically re-downloads GeoIP/GeoSite data files. Only matters if you use GEOIP/GEOSITE rules directly.

geo_update_interval.label: Geo update interval (hours)
geo_update_interval.desc: How often geo data auto-updates, in hours. 0 uses the default (24h).

enable.label: Built-in DNS
enable.desc: Uses the client's built-in DNS server. Must stay on for rule-based routing and fake-IP to work properly. When off, the device's system DNS is used.

listen.label: DNS listen
listen.desc: Address and port where the built-in DNS listens. TUN mode hijacks DNS to this address. Ports below 1024 (like 53) may need admin rights.

enhanced_mode.label: Enhanced mode
enhanced_mode.desc: fake-ip: returns a placeholder IP instantly, so connections start fast and the real lookup happens at the node with less DNS leakage (recommended). redir-host: resolves the real IP first; more compatible but slower and can leak. normal: plain DNS without enhancement.

fake_ip_range.label: Fake-IP range
fake_ip_range.desc: The range placeholder IPs are taken from in fake-IP mode. It must not overlap real networks. The default 198.18.0.1/16 is a reserved benchmark range and is safe.

fake_ip_filter_mode.label: Fake-IP filter mode
fake_ip_filter_mode.desc: How the fake-IP filter list is read. blacklist: listed domains get real IPs. whitelist: only listed domains get fake IPs. rule: entries are rules like RULE-SET,key,real-ip.

cache_algorithm.label: Cache algorithm
cache_algorithm.desc: How DNS answers are cached. lru evicts the least recently used; arc balances frequent and recent entries. Empty uses the client default.

ipv6.label: Return IPv6 (AAAA)
ipv6.desc: Whether DNS also answers with IPv6 (AAAA) records. Turn it off if IPv6 is off in the General tab.

respect_rules.label: DNS follows rules
respect_rules.desc: DNS queries themselves are routed by the rules, so a lookup for an overseas domain goes out through the matching node and avoids local DNS blocking. Requires proxy server nameservers to be set.

prefer_h3.label: Prefer HTTP/3 for DoH
prefer_h3.desc: Tries HTTP/3 (QUIC) first for DNS-over-HTTPS servers. Leave it off when UDP 443 is blocked (QUIC blocking on), since it would only add delay.

use_hosts.label: Use hosts
use_hosts.desc: Answers from the hosts list in the Advanced tab first.

use_system_hosts.label: Use system hosts
use_system_hosts.desc: Also answers from the device's system hosts file (/etc/hosts).

direct_nameserver_follow_policy.label: Direct NS follows policy
direct_nameserver_follow_policy.desc: Domains routed DIRECT are also resolved through the nameserver policy below. When off, only the direct nameservers are used.

default_nameserver.label: Bootstrap nameservers
default_nameserver.desc: DNS used to resolve the hostnames of DoH/DoT servers (e.g. dns.google). Must be plain IP addresses, one per line.

nameserver.label: Nameservers
nameserver.desc: Main DNS servers for normal lookups. Supports https:// (DoH), tls:// (DoT), quic:// (DoQ) and plain IPs, one per line. Several servers are queried at once and the fastest answer wins.

proxy_server_nameserver.label: Proxy server nameservers
proxy_server_nameserver.desc: DNS used only to resolve node (proxy server) hostnames. If this lookup is blocked the client cannot reach any node, so use DoH servers that are not blocked.

direct_nameserver.label: Direct nameservers
direct_nameserver.desc: DNS for domains that go DIRECT. 'system' uses the device's own DNS, which gives the nearest local servers.

fallback.label: Fallback nameservers
fallback.desc: Used instead of the main nameservers when an answer looks poisoned (see the fallback filter below). Usually overseas DoH servers. Can stay empty when respect-rules is on.

fake_ip_filter.label: Fake-IP exclusions
fake_ip_filter.desc: Domains that get real IPs instead of fake ones: router pages, game consoles, time sync and other services that need the real address. In rule mode, write RULE-SET,key,real-ip lines and end with MATCH,fake-ip.

nameserver_policy.label: Per-domain nameservers
nameserver_policy.desc: Resolves chosen domains with chosen DNS servers. One 'pattern = server1, server2' per line, e.g. '+.naver.com = system' or 'rule-set:kr_custom = https://1.1.1.1/dns-query' for a whole rule set.

ff_geoip.label: Judge by GeoIP
ff_geoip.desc: If an IP from the main nameservers is not in the country code below, treat it as poisoned and use the fallback answer.

ff_geoip_code.label: Trusted country code
ff_geoip_code.desc: Country used by the GeoIP check. With KR, any non-Korean answer is re-checked with the fallback servers.

ff_ipcidr.label: Poisoned IP ranges
ff_ipcidr.desc: Answers inside these ranges count as poisoned. One CIDR per line, e.g. 240.0.0.0/4.

ff_domain.label: Always-fallback domains
ff_domain.desc: These domains always skip the main nameservers and use the fallback servers. One per line, e.g. +.google.com.

enable.label: Enable sniffer
enable.desc: Reads TLS/HTTP headers of IP-only connections to recover the real domain, so domain rules still apply when an app connects straight to an IP.

force_dns_mapping.label: Sniff DNS-mapped
force_dns_mapping.desc: Also sniffs connections whose domain is already known from fake-IP or DNS records, to confirm the real domain.

parse_pure_ip.label: Sniff pure IP
parse_pure_ip.desc: Sniffs connections that carry no domain information at all, so hard-coded IP connections can still match domain rules.

override_destination.label: Override destination
override_destination.desc: Replaces the destination with the sniffed domain so the node resolves it itself. Off by default because some apps (pinned CDN IPs) can break.

http_override_destination.label: HTTP override destination
http_override_destination.desc: Applies destination override to HTTP connections only, independent of the setting above.

http_ports.label: HTTP ports
http_ports.desc: Ports where HTTP headers are read to find the domain. One per line; ranges like 8080-8880.

tls_ports.label: TLS ports
tls_ports.desc: Ports where the TLS SNI is read to find the domain. 443 and 8443 are usually enough.

quic_ports.label: QUIC ports
quic_ports.desc: Ports where QUIC (HTTP/3) is sniffed. Leave empty while QUIC blocking (UDP 443 reject) is on.

skip_domain.label: Skip domains
skip_domain.desc: Domains whose sniff results are ignored, for services that break when sniffed (e.g. Apple push). One per line; +. covers all subdomains.

force_domain.label: Force domains
force_domain.desc: Domains that are always sniffed regardless of other conditions. One per line.

skip_src_address.label: Skip source IPs
skip_src_address.desc: Connections from these source ranges are not sniffed. One CIDR per line.

skip_dst_address.label: Skip destination IPs
skip_dst_address.desc: Connections to these destination ranges are not sniffed. One CIDR per line.

hosts.label: Static hosts
hosts.desc: Pins domains to fixed IPs. One 'domain = IP' per line, e.g. router.lan = 192.168.0.1.

extra_yaml.label: Extra YAML
extra_yaml.desc: Any mihomo option not shown above (tun, ntp, experimental, ...) written as YAML. It is merged on top of the generated profile and wins on conflicts. proxies, proxy-groups, rules, rule-providers and proxy-providers are managed in their own tabs and cannot be set here.

settings.quicWarning: QUIC blocking (UDP 443 reject) is on, so QUIC sniffing has no effect.
settings.presetsHint: Pick a bundle and the related options are filled in at once. Nothing applies until you save, so feel free to try one.
settings.presetNote: Proxy groups, rules, hosts and extra YAML are not changed. Press Save afterwards to publish to subscriptions.

recommended.title: Recommended
recommended.desc: Stable settings that suit most users
recommended.detail: Sets mixed port 7890, rule mode, fake-ip DNS over Cloudflare/Google DoH, sniffer on, TCP concurrency and unified delay on. Choose this for a first setup or when unsure.

privacy.title: Privacy first
privacy.desc: No external controller, encrypted DNS only
privacy.detail: Recommended, plus the external controller and logs off, and every DNS query sent only over Quad9/Cloudflare encrypted DNS (DoH). The device's system DNS is not used.

compatible.title: Compatibility first
compatible.desc: When older apps or games fail to connect
compatible.detail: Returns real IPs with redir-host instead of fake-ip, and turns the sniffer and TCP concurrency off. Try this when a particular app, game or corporate network breaks. It can be slightly slower.

lowPower.title: Battery saver
lowPower.detail: Recommended, plus a 60-second keep-alive interval, concurrency and Geo auto-update off, and minimal logging. Dropped connections may be noticed a little later.

groupHint.ports: The proxy port the app opens on the device and how traffic is sent. One mixed port and Rule mode are usually enough.
groupHint.dnsBasic: How domain names become IPs. Keeping it on makes rule-based routing accurate and prevents DNS leaks.
groupHint.sniffBasic: Recovers the real domain of connections that arrive as bare IPs so domain rules still apply.
groupHint.extraPorts: Not needed with the mixed port. Open these only if an app supports HTTP-only or SOCKS5-only proxies.
groupHint.connection: Affects connection speed and how fast drops are noticed. Keep the defaults if unsure.
groupHint.app: The client app's logging, memory features and dashboard access.
groupHint.geo: Only matters if you write GEOIP/GEOSITE rules yourself. This profile uses rule sets (.mrs), so usually leave it off.
groupHint.dnsServers: Used top to bottom. Pick from the suggestions or type an address and press Enter. Pasting several lines adds them all.
groupHint.fakeIp: fake-ip answers instantly with a placeholder IP, which is fast, but some apps need the real IP. Put those domains in the filter.
groupHint.dnsPolicy: Sends specific domains to a different DNS server, for example local services to the device DNS (system).
groupHint.fallback: DNS used when the main answer looks poisoned. Leave empty to disable; adding one reveals the filter options below.
groupHint.sniffPorts: Domains are read from connections to these ports. 443 (HTTPS) and 80 (HTTP) cover most traffic.
groupHint.sniffExceptions: Exclude domains and addresses that break when sniffed, or force sniffing for specific domains.
groupHint.hosts: Pins a domain to an IP. Enter the domain on the left and the IP on the right, then add.
groupHint.extra: mihomo options not on this screen (tun, ntp, …) as raw YAML. The buttons insert common blocks, and syntax is checked as you type.

invalid.port: '{{value}}' is not a valid port. Use 443 or a range like 8080-8880.
invalid.cidr: '{{value}}' is not a valid address range. Use something like 192.168.0.0/16.

invalid.dns: '{{value}}' is not a valid DNS address. Use 1.1.1.1, https://…/dns-query, tls://… or system.

settings.dnsOff: DNS is off, so clients use the device DNS as-is. Domain rules become less accurate and DNS may leak.
settings.snifferOff: The sniffer is off, so domain rules do not apply to connections that arrive as bare IPs.
settings.extraMapping: The top level must be 'key: value' pairs, not a list or a single value.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: No. You pay once for the term you choose. Nothing is charged again when it ends; the plan simply expires.
faq.q2: What happens when I extend my current plan?
faq.a2: The new term is added after the time you have left. This month's usage and your monthly reset date stay the same.
faq.q3: What happens to my remaining time if I switch plans?
faq.a3: You move to the new plan as soon as you pay, and your remaining time carries over to it. Data usage starts again from zero.
faq.a4: Usage resets to zero on the same day each month, counted from the day your plan started. If you run out earlier, a reset ticket resets it immediately.
faq.a5: A coupon that sets this month's data usage back to zero right away. You can get one from promotions or support and use it in the Reset tickets section above.

subReset.whatBody: It's the address only for your account that your VPN app uses to fetch servers. Anyone who knows it can connect on your plan, so keep it private like a password.
subReset.when1: You see connections from devices or places you don't recognise
subReset.when2: You posted the link in a chat or forum by mistake
subReset.when3: You lost a device or gave it to someone
subReset.effectStopsBody: Every app using the current link stops receiving servers. Your own devices need the new link too.
subReset.effectKeepsBody: Your plan, remaining time, data usage and sign-in details don't change.
subReset.confirmCheck: I understand every app using the current link will disconnect and must be added again with the new link.
subReset.error: Couldn't reset the link. Please try again shortly.
subReset.doneTitle: Your new subscription link is ready
subReset.doneBody: The old link no longer works. Add the new link below to your devices again.
subReset.next2: In your VPN app, remove the old subscription and add the new link.
subReset.next3: Repeat on every device you use.
subReset.goDevices: Connect apps on the subscription page
